# Uniform local-output recovery for a supplied finite Gauss penalty

This source assembly combines a finite-time local-output estimate, a separately developed cutoff proof, a nonempty-sector corollary and a whole-term control budget for the declared periodic physical qubit family. The four mathematical bodies below are complete, attributed and byte-for-byte unchanged. Their original provisional or pending status sentences are historical records; the current, limited supervisory dispositions are the four exact acceptance records identified in `DEPENDENCIES.json`. This exact source composition is conditionally accepted under `01df29d92380b1e5a45d0c287a8b9044b7a588ac44612400793a768fa08322c7`; the publication rendering and driver require separate root review. This is not retained audit status. The actual finite-penalty publication parent is regular PR #9537 at head `eac18cba5c0699ef1c025fc77549bb682e35715e`.

**Current finite statement.** Let the coarse torus have even side length $L\ge4$, physical spacing 16 and physical period 16L. Use precisely the literal matter-edge qubits, disjoint hard-cutoff S=1 link pairs, ordered-prefix A words, B stars, background charge 3, positive local and Wilson cycle signs, and reducing precode $R_{0,L}$ defined in the appended sources. All idle physical qubits remain part of the physical tensor carrier. The common zero sector is $K_L=R_{0,L}\cap\ker\sum_xG_x^2$. The actual supplied Hamiltonian is $H_{\lambda,L}=\lambda N_{\mathrm{full},L}+B_L$, with positive penalty strength, the stated cycle/link/Gauss penalty, and the declared static coefficient budgets J, including real bare-stream couplings. The target remains the physical compressed Hamiltonian $B_{*,L}$ displayed in the cutoff proof. This statement does not replace it by an unproved all-volume fermion representation.

For every initial density operator supported on $K_L\otimes R$, every passive reference R, every physical output set S, and every forward time $t\ge0$, the direct proof gives, with

\[
k=57,\qquad c=60,\qquad g=(10+11\sqrt3)J,\qquad \lambda\ge16\pi kg,
\]

\[
\left\|\rho^{\rm full}_{S R}(t)-\rho^{\rm target}_{S R}(t)\right\|_1
\le\min\!\left\{2,\;8\pi c|S|\frac g\lambda
          \left[3e^{2kgt}-2\right]\right\}.
\]

This is full trace norm on the reduced output and the entire reference, including actual leakage; it uses no postselection, normalized block, product-state assumption or reference-dimension factor. The coefficient, support and output constants are independent of L. Uniformity means a common bound over the declared finite carriers, bounded output sizes, bounded gt, all allowed coefficient lists and all stated initial states. It is not global trace closeness, an all-time estimate or a construction of an infinite-volume state.

The full cycle/link penalty still belongs to the physical Hamiltonian. Its exact vanishing on the supplied reducing precode allows the comparison proof to use only the local integer Gauss penalty in the rotating frame. This reduction is a dynamical identity on that precode, not a removal of physical terms from the resource contract. The final fast rotation is charged through the enlarged physical observable support. The 57-site interaction supports, local incidence 11 and enlargement factor 60 are explicit conservative bounds; the model remains a supplied interaction with bounded but substantial arity and range.

**Nonempty family, with a limited conclusion.** The third proof supplies a neutral subspace inside the actual $K_L$, of dimension at least $20^{L^3}$ on the active carrier, for every even L≥4. It imposes all signed graph cycles as a stronger subcode and proves inclusion in the displayed local-plus-Wilson code. It does not assert equality of their cycle spans. Three occupied modes per cell are compatible with global even parity because L is even; each link may be in its zero-electric-field |00⟩ state. The odd-L parity conflict for this unchanged background remains explicit. No new parity carrier, preparation procedure or different Wilson sector is inserted.

**Two proof routes and their history.** Appendix A contains root's repaired direct proof (`fca3350c`), whose local commutator summation gives the displayed order-g/λ estimate at fixed gt. The first review found a factor-of-two inference gap in original `25b4a4fa`: its coarse substitution gave $6e^{2kgt}-5$, not $3e^{2kgt}-2$. V2 uses the stronger zero-mean periodic-primitive bound and retains the advertised constants. The complete original, exact delta, first review, subsequent source-exposed review and root disposition are preserved. The arithmetic defect is not misrepresented as a physical counterexample to the repaired dynamics.

Appendix B contains the alternative finite-neighborhood proof (`ac224bb8`). It proves its own two-sided finite-horizon local/reference estimate with enlargement factor 61, a summed commutator-path tail and a finite-neighborhood averaging term. Its stated logarithmic sixth-power loss and endpoint terms remain unchanged. It is an alternative proof, not a premise of Appendix A. The two original derivations had a shared root-supplied averaging route; the repaired direct source and later comparison are explicitly source-exposed. No blind or model-diverse validation is claimed.

Appendix C contains the accepted signed-cycle application (`2ddbcafc`), including its preserved 0/2/4 chord-incidence correction and even-parity condition. Generic connected-graph cycle/star machinery, commuting-penalty averaging and Lieb–Robinson methods are established tools. The signed application is included only to discharge nonemptiness of this declared finite family. The earlier [connected-graph encoding note](LOCAL_REFERENCE_FERMION_ENCODING_OBSTRUCTIONS_AND_CONSTRUCTIVE_GRAPH_ISOMETRIES_BOUNDED_THEOREM_NOTE_2026-09-14.md) is attribution context for its actually read graph sections, not an imported theorem from its unrelated obstruction sections. The averaging arguments here are supplied in full and import no unreturned literature appendix.

**Effective time and resources.** For $B_L=\kappa B_{0,L}$, $g=\kappa g_0$ and $t=\tau/\kappa$, the exponent depends on $g_0\tau$. The accepted direct-proof review gives the sufficient choice, for $g_0>0$, output size at most s≥1, finite forward effective horizon τ*, and $0<\epsilon\le2$,

\[
0<\kappa\le\min\!\left\{1,\frac{\lambda}{16\pi kg_0},
\frac{\epsilon\lambda}{8\pi c s g_0(3e^{2kg_0\tau_*}-2)}\right\}.
\]

Certified upper bounds on the denominator permit a smaller positive rational κ; stationary, empty-output and zero-time cases are handled directly. The physical time grows as $1/\kappa$. Nothing here claims efficient synthesis, state initialization, a clock or measurement apparatus, native two-site control, an odd/full-Fock loader, all-volume cubic covariance, a photon theory or a continuum limit.

Appendix D (`45ea7ab8`) proves, analytically for every even L≥4, the sufficient full-space physical whole-term budget

\[
\|H_{\lambda,\kappa,L}\|_{\rm local}
 \le166\lambda+(9+2\sqrt3)\kappa J_0.
\]

It uses conservative support covers of cardinality at most 32 and periodic physical L1 diameter at most 48. The physical drive coefficient β=9+2√3 differs from the expanded rotating-frame coefficient γ=10+11√3 used to bound the error. The literal scalar penalty coefficient $(43/4)L^3 I$ remains inside the physical terms; the total Hamiltonian need not be positive. This is an explicit whole-term interaction budget, including cycle/link terms which vanish dynamically on the precode. The sharper resolved Pauli penalty coefficient 43/2 in the finite-penalty parent is an L=4 result and is not extended by this assembly.

For a supplied positive whole-term cap Λ, J₀>0, and the same finite s, τ* and ε, Appendix D gives the sufficient common choice

\[
\lambda=\Lambda/332,\qquad
0<\kappa\le\min\!\left\{1,\frac{\Lambda}{2(9+2\sqrt3)J_0},
\frac{\lambda}{16\pi kg_0},
\frac{\epsilon\lambda}{8\pi c s g_0(3e^{2kg_0\tau_*}-2)}\right\},
\quad g_0=(10+11\sqrt3)J_0.
\]

This bounds the full physical site budget by Λ and the reduced output/reference error by ε simultaneously over the declared even finite volumes, allowed coefficient lists, all initial states in $K_L\otimes R$, output sets with at most s sites, and forward effective times $0\le\tau\le\tau_*$. The target is the same physical compressed $B_{0,*,L}$ evolution at τ. The frozen budget source leaves nonemptiness supplied; this composition uses Appendix C explicitly to discharge that premise for the stated family. Existence of its neutral subcode does not prepare any input, identify the full displayed code, or establish an all-volume CAR/cubic action. Exact static multi-qubit controls and coefficient setting remain supplied. Certified parameter selection is not a robustness theorem for arbitrary rounding of penalties or a physical clock/precision resource construction.

**Premises and evidence.** The [finite-penalty note](FINITE_GAUSS_PENALTY_RECOVERY_BOUNDED_THEOREM_NOTE_2026-10-14.md) supplies the literal bare perturbation, reducing precode, compression and finite-penalty context; its current canonical SHA-256 is `437f2f4e94aa93038173cd138c5f6b9ad4ebdc4fbc7416428cfa13192c9e4ff4`, bound to actual regular [PR #9537](https://github.com/jonathonreilly/qubit-lattice-axiom-framework/pull/9537). The [joint-interface note](JOINT_EVEN_MATTER_FINITE_LINK_INTERFACE_BOUNDED_THEOREM_NOTE_2026-10-14.md), canonical `212a94bb` with original core `34cbe355`, supplies literal geometry and operator definitions. The two original complete bodies are archived with their exact hashes. These are scientific uses of source bodies; no dependency is inferred from branch ancestry and no graph edge or root count is prescribed.

The archive preserves the complete relevant proof/review directories, original failures and actual control streams, deduplicated by content hash. The cutoff control uses two physical qubits and an entangled reference, with wrong-sign, omitted-fast-frame, omitted-primitive and missing-commutator-factor discriminators. The graph control is a six-edge finite graph, with a positive cycle relation, flipped-character and odd-parity controls. The budget control uses only selected L=4 and 6 binary supports and incidences; it preserves the failed naive triangle-cover route and does not compute phases, ranks or a resolved Pauli norm. Those selected controls neither establish the analytic local bound nor census all L. The budget acceptance is a source-exposed root review, and the assembly adds no model-diverse validation. The present assembly runs only deterministic source identity, extraction and preservation checks; these report zero mathematical predicates. Root retains mathematical composition, driver and publication acceptance. This directory is a source-preparation artifact, not a competing operational checkpoint.
